title: Trying to reassign a reactiveVal to the name of an existing reactiveVal doesn't overwrite the latter
rationale: Facts: reporter BajczA475 shows that rebinding a name to a new reactiveVal() (e.g. inside an observeEvent reset handler) does not invalidate observers subscribed to the original reactiveVal, leaving 'silent failure states'; reporter states upfront they don't believe it's a bug. Classification hypothesis: documentation gap, not a bug -- maintainer gadenbuie confirmed in-thread that this is standard signal/subscription semantics (the old reactive value never receives an invalidation signal when the name is rebound) and walked through three correct alternatives (mutate then rebind, destroy via internals, or module self-destruct). Duplicate search: none found among currently scanned issues; this is a fresh docs request, not a repeat bug report. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shiny's own reactiveVal() docs. Regression check: not applicable -- both reporter and maintainer agree this is longstanding, intentional behavior, not a behavior change. Reproduction plan: already provided and confirmed by the maintainer; no further repro needed. Impact: low -- purely a documentation clarity gap; the reporter (5 years of Shiny experience) was tripped up and proposed exact wording for the Details section of reactiveVal()'s help page, which a maintainer can drop in directly. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; this is a well-scoped, maintainer-endorsed documentation fix with proposed text already in the thread, safe to label without further review.

title: Modals show below full-screened cards
rationale: Facts: reporter bastianolea provides a minimal shiny+bslib reprex (page_fillable + full_screen card + showModal()) showing that opening a modal while a bslib card is full-screened renders the modal below/behind the full-screen overlay instead of on top of it; reporter notes showNotification() correctly layers above the full-screen card, suggesting a z-index gap specific to modals. Classification hypothesis: bug -- a CSS stacking-context defect, most plausibly a z-index mismatch between shiny's modal dialog and bslib's full-screen card overlay. Duplicate search: no matching open issue found among currently scanned candidates. Wrong-location check: ambiguous between shiny (owns the modal dialog CSS) and bslib (owns the full-screen card overlay CSS); reporter argues shiny since notifications already stack correctly, but the root cause could live in either package's z-index values, so 'wrong location' is not confidently assignable without a maintainer inspecting both stylesheets -- filed in the repo whose component (the modal) is failing to stack correctly, which is a reasonable default. Regression check: no evidence given that this differed in an older release; not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: complete and minimal -- the provided reprex is sufficient to reproduce and diagnose without further reprex requests. Impact: moderate -- affects any app combining a full-screen bslib card with a shiny modal, making the modal effectively inaccessible in that state; a workaround (exit full-screen before opening a modal) likely exists. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; a clear, reproducible visual bug with moderate impact and a plausible workaround, safe to label without further review.

title: Input not updating after `session$destroy` if value matches default when destroyed
rationale: Facts: reporter JamesStewartRE provides a deterministic, fully self-contained reprex (built on the session$destroy() capability added in #4372) showing that after removeUI + session$destroy() + insertUI + re-running a module server, a statically-defined selectInput's server-side input value becomes NULL specifically when the previously selected value matches the recreated UI's default -- described with exact step-by-step expected vs. actual behavior. Classification hypothesis: bug in the relatively new session$destroy()/module-recreation code path, not a regression from older stable behavior since session$destroy() is itself a new feature. Duplicate search: reporter explicitly distinguishes this from #4416 (which asks to preserve statically-defined inputs entirely) -- this issue is about an inconsistency introduced specifically by the destroy/recreate flow, not a duplicate. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- session$destroy() and module lifecycle are shiny-core concerns. Regression check: no evidence of differing behavior versus an older released version (the underlying capability is new), so not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: complete, deterministic, and already provided; no further reprex needed. Impact: moderate -- affects apps that dynamically tear down and recreate modules with statically-defined inputs, producing input state that unpredictably depends on whether the user changed the value before recreation; workaround (always changing the value, or using unique IDs) is awkward but exists. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; a clear, high-confidence, deterministic repro with moderate scoped impact, safe to label without further review.

title: page_navbar() pages are missing banner and main landmarks
rationale: Facts: reporter jcheng5 (Shiny team) documents that page_navbar()/navbarPage() renders only a bare <nav> for its top bar (no <header>/banner landmark) and, when no sidebar is supplied, wraps content in a plain <div class="container-fluid"> instead of a <main> landmark -- contrasted with the sidebar case, which already gets a <main> via page_main_container(). Classification hypothesis: accessibility bug -- missing ARIA/HTML landmark regions that screen-reader users rely on for page navigation via a landmark rotor. Duplicate search: none found among currently scanned candidates. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- bslib owns page_navbar() and page_main_container(); reporter correctly scopes the fix to page_navbar() rather than the shared navs_bar_()/navbarPage_() helpers, since navset_bar() can be embedded anywhere and page-level landmarks would be inappropriate there. Regression check: not applicable -- this is a pre-existing gap, not a behavior change from an older release. Reproduction plan: not a runtime repro but a precise, independently verifiable DOM-structure comparison (page_navbar() output vs. page_main_container()'s sidebar-case output); sufficient to act on without a reprex app. Impact: moderate-to-significant -- affects every page_navbar() app for screen-reader users, who lose banner/main landmark navigation entirely (only 'navigation' currently appears in the landmark rotor); filed by a core maintainer with a precise, actionable fix scope. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; a precise, maintainer-authored accessibility fix request, safe to label without further review.

title: export() raises UnicodeEncodeError and interpolate_file() returns a corrupted prompt when the locale is not UTF-8
rationale: Facts: reporter ebarkhordar shows that under a non-UTF-8 locale (e.g. LC_ALL=en_US.ISO-8859-1), chat.export() raises UnicodeEncodeError for both .md and .html output containing non-ASCII text, while interpolate_file() fails silently -- it returns a mojibake-corrupted prompt rather than raising, and even warns that comparing the string visually in a non-UTF-8 terminal re-encodes back to the original bytes and can mask the bug. Reproduction requires no API key and is confirmed against chatlas 0.23.0 (PyPI) and main (7b3aa56). Classification hypothesis: bug -- an encoding-handling defect, most concerning in interpolate_file() because it fails silently rather than raising. Duplicate search: none found among currently scanned candidates. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- chatlas' own export() and interpolate_file() implementations. Regression check: no evidence given that this differed in an older chatlas release; not labeled regression. Reproduction plan: complete, minimal, deterministic, and dependency-free (no API key); no further reprex needed. Impact: moderate -- limited to non-UTF-8 locale environments, but reporter notes this is plausible on Windows (cp1252 default) and any container with an unset/non-UTF-8 locale, and the silent corruption in interpolate_file() means affected users may not notice until a prompt reaches the model garbled. Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; a clear, well-isolated, dependency-free repro of a real correctness bug, safe to label without further review.

title: feat(pkg-r): use ellmer::content_document_url() for text attachments
rationale: Facts: reporter kaipingyang shows that content_from_attachment() hand-assembles a string for text-based attachments while images/PDFs already go through ellmer content constructors, and proposes replacing the text branch with ellmer's newer content_document_url(mime_type=...) (added in ellmer 0.5.0), citing benefits (uniform code path, native document handling by providers, less manual HTML escaping) and offering to send a PR; verified against ellmer 0.5.0.9000. Classification hypothesis: feature/refactor request, not a bug -- current behavior works, this is a consistency and quality improvement. Duplicate search: none found among currently scanned candidates. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat's own content_from_attachment() (R package). Regression check: not applicable -- no prior behavior regressed. Reproduction plan: not applicable to a feature request; the proposed code diff is self-contained and verifiable by inspection. Impact: low -- a well-reasoned, low-risk refactor, but explicitly raises the minimum ellmer version floor to >= 0.5.0 for the R package, which is a deliberate maintainer/dependency-policy decision rather than an urgent fix. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; a well-specified, low-risk enhancement proposal with an offered PR, safe to label without further review.

title: Include `title` in single citation cards
rationale: Facts: reporter gadenbuie (maintainer) shows via screenshots that a citation pill with a title shows that title when multiple citations collapse into one pill, but not in the single-citation case; a side investigation into multi-line markdown inside <shiny-aside> tags was raised in a follow-up comment and then retracted after further testing showed multi-line markdown already works correctly on main. The same maintainer's final comment states the single-citation title-display gap 'is addressed separately: the popover now always repeats the aside's full label/title,' indicating the fix may already be in progress or landed. Classification hypothesis: minor UI-consistency bug (cosmetic). Duplicate search: none found among currently scanned candidates; the multi-line markdown tangent was self-resolved by the same reporter, not a separate issue. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat's own citation/aside rendering. Regression check: not applicable -- this is a display-consistency gap, not a behavior change from an older release. Reproduction plan: screenshots provided are sufficient; no further reprex needed. Impact: low -- purely cosmetic pill/popover title display, already being actively worked by the reporting maintainer. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; low-impact, maintainer-owned, and apparently already in progress -- per rubric this workflow does not auto-close, so a human should close it once the maintainer confirms the fix landed.

title: Drawer takeover threshold ignores configured drawer width
rationale: Facts: reporter cpsievert (maintainer) documents with exact file/line references that the chat drawer's full-width takeover uses a fixed 640px threshold (js/src/chat/ChatContainer.tsx) derived from minimum widths, while the drawer's actual resolved width can be configured much wider (e.g. 720px via querychat's calc(min(clamp(360px, 55vw, 720px), 100%))), producing a cramped side-by-side layout across the ~640-1100px viewport band before takeover finally triggers; provides a concrete measured example table, a proposed dynamic-threshold formula, an implementation sketch spanning JS/SCSS, and an open API decision (drag-resize clamping) with a stated preference. Classification hypothesis: bug in the responsive layout's takeover logic -- the threshold doesn't account for the drawer's configured/requested width. Duplicate search: none found among currently scanned candidates. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- shinychat owns ChatContainer.tsx and the drawer takeover CSS/JS. Regression check: not applicable -- the fixed-threshold assumption has existed since the feature was designed, not a change from a previously-correct behavior. Reproduction plan: a concrete, already-observed real-world case (querychat's configured drawer) plus a measured viewport/width table stand in for a runnable reprex; sufficient to act on. Impact: moderate -- affects any app configuring a drawer wider than the built-in minimum assumptions, degrading the layout across a meaningful viewport band; already affecting a known downstream consumer (querychat). Priority: Medium. Recommended next action: label Priority: Medium and mark ai-triage:done; a precise, maintainer-authored bug report with a concrete fix proposal, safe to label without further review.

title: Doc markdown not rendering properly
rationale: Facts: reporter schloerke (maintainer) provides a screenshot of the input_task_button() API doc page showing the literal HTML entity `"` rendered in place of a decoded `"` character, and suggests adding a test plus possibly a whitelist of allowable escapings to catch unexpected double-escaping in the docs pipeline. Classification hypothesis: bug -- an HTML-entity double-escaping defect in the documentation/markdown rendering pipeline. Duplicate search: none found among currently scanned candidates. Wrong-location check: correct repo -- py-shiny owns its own API doc generation. Regression check: no explicit before/after comparison against an older released version is given, so not labeled regression despite being plausible. Reproduction plan: no runnable repro or specific source markdown snippet is included, only a screenshot and the affected doc URL -- thinner than a typical external bug report, but filed directly by the maintainer who owns the doc pipeline and can inspect the source directly; not requesting needs reprex given the self-filed, directly-actionable nature of the report. Impact: low -- a cosmetic documentation rendering defect (stray literal entity in rendered text), not a functional or data-integrity issue. Priority: Low. Recommended next action: label Priority: Low and mark ai-triage:done; a low-risk, cosmetic docs defect self-filed by the maintainer who owns the fix, safe to label without further review.
